comment: D-STATE-1. One `{id, name, at}` record -- the shape `recents[]`,
`lastPlayed` and `session` all share -- run by BOTH tests/Model.test.js
(normalize_played). A rule implemented in two languages gets one fixture.
This file exists because the two DID disagree. Model.js coerces with
Math.trunc(Number(x)), which parses the whole JavaScript numeric grammar;
the helper used int(x), which accepts only a plain integer literal and
raises on everything else, falling through to 0. Same bytes, two answers.
Found by the saved-search fixture, which included `at: "12.9"` for its own
key and went red on a key it was not written for -- the shared-fixture rule
working on a rule nobody had applied it to yet.
The agreed answer is Model.js's, for two reasons. It is the reader the
guide runs, so it is what the user's screen already reflects; and it is the
more tolerant of the two, so adopting it cannot turn a value that used to
be read into one that is not.
atComment: Every vector is `at` on an otherwise valid record. `want` is what BOTH readers must return.

at.why: integer, the shape both writers actually emit
string integer, agreed before this fix
leading zeros are not octal in either reader
surrounding whitespace, agreed before this fix
float truncates toward zero, agreed before this fix
negative float truncates TOWARD ZERO, not down
D-STATE-1: JS read 12, the helper raised and stored 0
D-STATE-1: JS read -3, the helper raised and stored 0
D-STATE-1: exponent notation, JS read 1000, the helper 0
a number with a tail is NOT 7 in either reader
boolean, agreed before this fix and pinned so it stays agreed

recordComment: Whole-record vectors: a record without an id is not a record, on both sides.
nonNegativeComment: D-STATE-1 was filed against the played record alone and was never only there. `non_negative_int` / the JS source-record reader carry the SAME coercion on five more keys -- addedAt, lastUsed, fetchedAt, channelCount, groupCount -- and had the same disagreement. Same vectors, then clamped at zero.

nonNegative.why: D-STATE-1 again: JS read 12, the helper 0
clamped at zero, which is the only difference from `at`
negative after truncation is still clamped
